title: Caching: why changing the seed does not reload the model

questions.q: You change only the seed. Which nodes run again in the standard graph?
options: The sampler and everything downstream of it
questions.answer: The sampler and everything downstream of it
questions.why: The seed is part of the sampler's signature and so of every descendant's. Ancestors keep their keys.

questions.q: You rename every node id. What happens?
questions.why: Ancestors are numbered by position, so ids are not part of the key, except for not-idempotent nodes and those taking UNIQUE_ID.

questions.q: What does a fingerprint of float("NaN") do?
options: Makes the node run every time, because NaN never equals itself
questions.answer: Makes the node run every time, because NaN never equals itself
questions.why: A key holding NaN cannot match a stored key.

questions.q: What is the default cache policy in v0.43.0?
questions.why: main.py sets CacheType.RAM_PRESSURE unless --cache-classic, --cache-lru or --cache-none is given.

questions.q: Two ordinary nodes have identical class and inputs. What happens?
options: They have the same key, so they share one result
The second one is an error
questions.answer: They have the same key, so they share one result
questions.why: The lab shows equal keys. Not-idempotent nodes add their id to avoid exactly this.
